summary: Ephemeral job preemption causing intermittent batched throughput sag in dedicated cluster
description: Issue summary: BrightLedger reported repeated windows of reduced batched throughput (p50 throughput drop ~30%, p95 latency increase 3x) on their dedicated pool in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-11T23:00Z. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints saw elevated tail latency and reduced tokens/sec for multi-request batched routes. Scope: affects ~3 GPU nodes in BrightLedger's reserved pool, intermittent (2–10 minute windows) and correlated with transient ephemeral jobs scheduled in the same cluster. Timeline: 2026-03-11 23:01 – first alert from synthetic checks; 23:03 — customer report; 23:10 — support triage; 23:35 — mitigation throttle applied; 2026-03-12 — engineering investigation ongoing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a dedicated pool with reserved GPUs (BrightLedger config).
2) Launch steady inference traffic using batched routes (batch target 8, max latency 250ms).
3) Submit short-lived ephemeral training/instrumentation jobs that create heavy CPU+IO on nodes concurrently (simulated background job in test harness).
4) Observe autoscaler and scheduler logs during bursts; monitor p95 latency and tokens/sec for the serving runtime.
observed_behavior: - Short, repeated windows (2-10m) where token throughput drops ~25-35% and p95 latency rises from ~140ms to ~420ms for batched endpoints.
- GPU allocations show no OOMs, but scheduling logs contain preemption/eviction events for low-priority ephemeral pods (kube-scheduler).
- Node-level metrics show CPU steal and iowait spikes during windows; NVLink and GPU memory stable.
- Autoscaler response lags: new pods created but batching doesn't recover immediately due to KV cache warming and batch serialization.
expected_behavior: Dedicated pool should preserve batched throughput for reserved tenants. Background ephemeral jobs on best-effort tenants should not induce intermittent p99/p95 regressions for reserved capacity customers.
logs: kubelet evict events (2026-03-11T23:02:14Z): preempted pod ephemeral-ia-224 - reason: "Preemption by higher-priority burst"
serving-runtime trace (2026-03-11T23:02:18Z): batch_worker stall detected: wait_for_batch() duration 340ms (normal 40-60ms)
node metrics snippet (iowait): node-az3-004 iowait jump 0.4 -> 3.7 (23:02-23:05)
autoscaler log: scale_up triggered but new pods returned NotReady for 45s due to sidecar init and kv-cache restore
comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12T00:10Z: Acknowledged receipt from customer. Reproduced transient drop in staging by running bursty ephemeral jobs. Escalating to SRE for scheduler/autoscaler correlation.

SRE (Luis Ortega) 2026-03-12T01:05Z: Observed preemption chains in kube-scheduler; ephemeral jobs are not constrained and spike node CPU/IO. Scheduling preemption causes pod restarts on reserved nodes and disrupts surviving batchers.
Customer (BrightLedger - Alex Cho) 2026-03-12T01:30Z: We observed production errors during scheduled batch windows; requesting mitigation and ETA for fix. Impacting customer SLAs.
Infra (SRE) 2026-03-12T03:20Z: Temporary mitigation applied: added taint on dedicated nodes to repel best-effort ephemeral scheduling and set eviction thresholds; monitoring for recurrence.
Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12T04:00Z: Customer notified of temporary mitigation; asked to validate if throughput stabilizes during their peak window tonight.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: noisy best-effort ephemeral jobs consume CPU/io bandwidth causing kubelet/cgroup contention and triggering preemptions that serialize batched requests.
Hypothesis B: autoscaler cooldown and kv-cache restore time combine to create a recovery hole; new nodes join but batchers are cold, lowering effective throughput.
Finding: Eviction logs match timing of throughput drops. Node iowait and CPU steal correlate with eviction windows. No GPU memory contention or thermal events found.
Supporting artifacts: correlated grafana dashboard panels (requests/sec, tokens/sec, node iowait, kube-scheduler preemption_rate) show tight coupling of events.
Attempted reproducer in staging: reproduced by running 10s ephemeral CPU+disk IO spikes; same pattern of eviction -> batch stall -> autoscaler lag observed.
Short-term mitigation verified in canary: tainting dedicated nodes prevented ephemeral pods from scheduling and removed the 10m windows in canary traffic.

Long-term options considered: (1) enforce node-level QoS/CPU and IO limits for best-effort tenants; (2) introduce preemption-aware placement (reserved instance isolation); (3) tune autoscaler to pre-warm nodes or reduce kv-cache restore time via checkpoint sharing.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-12): added a dedicated-node taint + updated scheduler tolerations for BrightLedger's pool to prevent best-effort ephemeral jobs from landing on reserved GPUs. This eliminated recurrence in canary. Next steps: SRE and Scheduler team to implement a policy change: set soft-affinity for reserved pools, enforce CPU/iowait quotas on sidecars, and reduce kv-cache warm time by sharing checkpoints across pod starts. Follow-up action items created: GH issue infra#2246 for autoscaler prewarm, runbook update to prevent ephemeral job escalation. Target date for permanent mitigation: 2026-03-19.
